evidence.claim: Sowing window. 10 Nov to 30 Nov
evidence.crop_context: Wheat / Bread wheat for grain
evidence.limitations: Regional evidence. Match locality, variety and farm constraints.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C01. Candidate only

evidence.claim: Physiological maturity window. 15 Apr to 10 May
evidence.crop_context: Wheat / Bread wheat for grain
evidence.limitations: Maturity differs from crop removal and field release.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C02. Candidate maturity window only

evidence.claim: Trial sowing dates. 5 Nov, 5 Dec, 5 Jan. Highest-yield treatments differed by genotype.
evidence.crop_context: Wheat / Misr 3, Sakha 94, Gemmiza 12, Sids 14, Shandaweel 1 and five other genotypes
evidence.limitations: Experimental dates are discrete treatments, not a continuous eligibility interval.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C03. Use to inform cultivar review

evidence.claim: Time to physiological maturity. 15 Nov sowing yielded 152.0 and 153.3 days. 30 Nov sowing yielded 140.0 and 138.0 days.
evidence.crop_context: Wheat / Sakha 95 bread wheat
evidence.locator: Experimental site and Table 6, Sakha 95 rows
evidence.limitations: Study-specific treatment means. Field release and sowing conditions differ.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C04. Candidate duration evidence

evidence.claim: Local crop-coefficient evidence. Initial 0.43–0.68, development 0.75–1.02, mid 0.94–1.11, end 0.40–0.64
evidence.crop_context: Wheat / Pilot cultivar unspecified
evidence.limitations: Measured ETa divided by FAO ET₀. Wetting, cultivar, site conditions and stage mapping need confirmation. Full paper unavailable in this review.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C05. Candidate coefficients only

evidence.claim: Standard Kc references. Spring wheat uses cereal-group initial 0.30, mid 1.15, end 0.25–0.40. For winter wheat on non-frozen soil FAO lists initial 0.70.
evidence.crop_context: Wheat / Spring-habit grain wheat versus winter-habit wheat
evidence.locator: Table 12, cereals, spring and winter wheat, footnote 10
evidence.limitations: Winter sowing does not determine growth habit. Match moisture/harvest and initial wetting.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C06. Choose reviewed curve, never average rows

evidence.claim: Sowing guidance. Early to mid-October preferred, with mid-September to end-October described as broader guidance
evidence.crop_context: Berseem / Egyptian clover forage
evidence.limitations: Check local weather, predecessor harvest and type. University guidance does not define Sakha cutoffs.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C07. Candidate only

evidence.claim: Cutting type. Fahl single-cut, Meskawi multi-cut
evidence.crop_context: Berseem / Fahl versus Meskawi/Miscawi
evidence.limitations: Record intended forage or seed use. A seed crop can occupy the field beyond a forage cut.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C08. Verify farmer type before counting cuts

evidence.claim: First cut and interval guidance. First 50–55 days after sowing, then 25–30 between cuts
evidence.crop_context: Berseem / Regrowing forage types
evidence.limitations: Temperature, establishment, irrigation and regrowth matter. The teaching range cannot fix a promise date.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C09. Inform interview only

evidence.claim: Five-cut trial schedule. First at 50 days, then intervals 45, 40, 35, 30
evidence.crop_context: Berseem / Gemiza 1, Sakha 4, Helali, Giza 6, Serw 1
evidence.limitations: Published management protocol, different from the university course. No universal cycle length.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C10. Inactivate as a general rule

evidence.claim: Time to final cut. 200 = 50 + 45 + 40 + 35 + 30
evidence.crop_context: Berseem / Five-cut trial above
evidence.locator: Materials and methods, derived from the five intervals
evidence.limitations: Final cut is not equivalent to first free day. No evidence here for a sixth cut or release interval.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C11. Trial context only

evidence.claim: Lock and field release. Obtain protected cuts/dates, intended use, last cut, first free day and prep interval
evidence.crop_context: Berseem / Farmer’s named variety and purpose
evidence.limitations: Ceasing cutting early, grazing, regrowth or seed retention can change occupancy. Feed quantity unknown.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C12. Leave critical missing commitment unresolved

evidence.claim: Standard seasonal and cutting-cycle Kc. Averaged cuts 0.40/0.90/0.85. Individual cycles 0.40/1.15/1.10.
evidence.crop_context: Berseem / Berseem clover hay
evidence.locator: Table 12, Clover hay, Berseem, footnotes 13–14, Fig. 35
evidence.limitations: Cycle points are after cut, full cover, before cut. Local fresh forage, timing and water regime require review.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C13. Seasonal ETc conditional, extra-cut savings unavailable

evidence.claim: Sowing window. 15 Apr to 15 May
evidence.crop_context: Maize / Grain production, hybrid to be confirmed
evidence.limitations: Atlas labels maize. Corroborate grain purpose with the Sakha grain trial and named hybrid.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C14. Candidate only

evidence.claim: Duration. Early about 100, medium/late 110–130
evidence.crop_context: Maize / Early and medium/late maturity groups
evidence.locator: Table 1, Nile Delta, maize and definitions
evidence.limitations: Grain moisture, actual harvest and residue removal determine release.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C15. Apply only after hybrid/purpose review

evidence.claim: Sowing-date comparison. 15 May, 15 Jun and 15 Jul tested during 2023–24. SC168 performed best at 15 May within trial.
evidence.crop_context: Maize / SC131, SC168, TWC324 for grain
evidence.limitations: Trial dates are not a general June–July window. Preserve study conditions.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C16. Context for hybrid review

evidence.claim: Standard Kc references. Initial cereal-group 0.30, mid 1.20, end 0.60 high-moisture grain or 0.35 drier field grain
evidence.crop_context: Maize / Field maize for grain
evidence.limitations: Wetting, height, stage durations and dry-down matter. Exclude sweet corn and silage rows.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C17. Select endpoints only for matched management

evidence.claim: Local water regime and coefficients. 0.43, 0.54, 0.64, 0.58, 0.51 in five successive phases
evidence.crop_context: Maize / SC10 grain maize
evidence.locator: Table 9 and discussion, five phases from emergence to maturity
evidence.limitations: Ratios reflect treatment and stage definitions. They do not directly fill the four FAO stages.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C18. Context for sensitivity only

evidence.claim: Nonlocal sowing/harvest evidence. 20 Apr to 15 May sowing and 1–30 Aug harvest
evidence.crop_context: Grain sorghum / Sorghum in regional calendar
evidence.limitations: Atlas does not specify this row for the Nile Delta or confirm the pilot cultivar.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C19. Keep out of Sakha eligibility

evidence.claim: Experimental planting dates. 7 Apr, 27 Apr, 17 May, 6 Jun, 26 Jun
evidence.crop_context: Grain sorghum / Shandaweel-1, -305, -306 and Dorado
evidence.limitations: Out-of-area trial. Paper differs between abstract and methods on the second study year. Dates of sowing agree.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C20. Research context only

evidence.claim: Time to grain harvest. 91/85/76 and 92/86/74 for the three tested dates across the two years
evidence.crop_context: Grain sorghum / Shandaweel-1, Shandaweel-2, Durado (author spelling)
evidence.limitations: Experiment reports time to harvest. Population, climate, timing and soils differ from Sakha.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C21. No transfer to Sakha occupancy

evidence.claim: Crop-purpose exclusion. Sowing/cutting evidence concerns forage
evidence.crop_context: Grain sorghum / Sakha forage sorghum experiment
evidence.limitations: Location matches but yield endpoint and cutting management differ from grain.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C22. Exclude forage rules from grain path

evidence.claim: Pilot sowing, occupancy and Kc activation. Local planting window, time to grain harvest, stage timing and release undetermined
evidence.crop_context: Grain sorghum / Locally suitable grain cultivar unidentified
evidence.locator: Nile Delta versus Upper Egypt rows, compare C20–C22
evidence.limitations: Regional national evidence and a local forage study do not establish a Sakha grain sequence.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C23. Inactive until local grain-specific evidence

evidence.claim: Standard Kc reference. Cereal-group initial 0.30, mid 1.00–1.10, end 0.55
evidence.crop_context: Grain sorghum / Grain, distinct from sweet or forage
evidence.limitations: Reviewed local stages, variety and moisture management absent.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C24. Withhold Sakha ETc

evidence.claim: Preparation and harvest logistics. First free day and preparation duration currently unknown
evidence.crop_context: All four / Named cultivar and field
evidence.limitations: No cross-crop universal turnaround identified. Do not use zero as an automatic default.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C25. Critical missing input prevents eligibility

evidence.claim: Soil compatibility and irrigation access. No approved local numeric salinity, pH, drainage or texture exclusion. Canal and access constraints require confirmation.
evidence.crop_context: All four / Field-specific soil and irrigation
evidence.locator: Methodology 1, soil restrictions and evidence source
evidence.limitations: Keep laboratory measurement, farmer description and unknown separate. Irrigation water EC and soil-extract EC are different.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C26. Inactive thresholds, retain unresolved critical conditions

evidence.claim: Rotation/sequence indicators. Track repeated cereal family and berseem legume placement
evidence.crop_context: All four / Three cereals and one legume
evidence.locator: Methodology 1, family repetition and legume placement
evidence.limitations: A sequence indicator alone cannot quantify soil change, nitrogen gain or impose a universal ban.
evidence.notes: Crop ledger C27. Display indicator, require evidence for binding restriction
